subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Global vs. Local Sourcing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Global vs. Local Sourcing.

hook.text: A factory in China makes parts for 40% less. But the lead time is 8 weeks and shipping costs are rising.

buildup.text: Global sourcing taps lower-cost markets worldwide. Local sourcing prioritizes nearby suppliers for speed.

discovery.text: Global sourcing saves on unit cost. Local sourcing saves on lead time, transport, and supply risk.

twist.text: The total landed cost of global sourcing often exceeds local options once tariffs, shipping, and delays are added.

climax.text: Nearshoring—sourcing from nearby countries—is booming as companies balance cost, speed, and resilience.

punchline.text: Cheap overseas isn't always cheap when it lands at your dock.

quiz.question: What is nearshoring?
options: Buying from the cheapest global supplier
Sourcing from nearby countries to balance cost and speed
